text:
tilly: Hi team — ACME (customer) reporting intermittent Go SDK stream parse failures. Root error: "unexpected EOF" when decoding JSON from Stream(), only on heavy payloads. Logs attached by customer.
acme-app: repro steps: we call `client.Stream(ctx, req)` and then use `bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)` to read lines and `json.Unmarshal(scanner.Bytes(), &evt)`. Happens after ~30s, last object truncated mid-json. curl works (we get full objects).\nacme-app: our module: `github.com/redwood-inference/go-client v0.2.0` and example code copied from README.
mike: likely bufio.Scanner limit (default 64k token). If a single NDJSON line >64KB scanner.Err() will return `token too long`. Also scanner won't combine across chunk boundaries. Which exact error are you seeing? `unexpected EOF` suggests decode on partial bytes.
acme-app: error in logs shows `json: unexpected end of JSON input` from `json.Unmarshal`. No explicit scanner token too long; looks like partial last chunk.
nana (typo corrected): sorry for noise — tagging eng-runtime.
nana (eng-runtime): server side: we emit chunked Transfer-Encoding with each event as a single JSON object followed by `\n`. However large fields (e.g., base64 embeddings) can produce very large single-line events. Some proxies (nginx) can cut chunk boundaries differently; curl is more permissive because it reassembles.
mike: two mitigation paths: 1) keep using a scanner but increase buffer: `scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 1024*64), 1024*1024*5)` to allow tokens up to 5MB; 2) avoid scanner and use `json.Decoder` to stream decode from `io.Reader` which handles arbitrary object sizes across chunks. Example:

```
dec := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body)
for {
  var evt Event
  if err := dec.Decode(&evt); err == io.EOF { break }
  if err != nil { log.Printf("decoding: %v", err); break }
  handle(evt)
}
```

This doesn't rely on single-line framing.\nkevin: also check client Transport settings and any intermediary proxies — some NGiNX configs with `proxy_buffering` or `proxy_request_buffering` can affect chunking. If client retries due to connection resets you might see truncated reads.
mike: agreed. For the SDK: plan is to add a defensive fallback — try NDJSON Scanner first (for backcompat), on token-too-large or decode errors fall back to `json.Decoder` streaming. We'll also increase default scanner buffer to 512KB and make it configurable. We'll emit telemetry tag `stream.parse_mode` (scanner|decoder) and `stream.truncated` for investigation.
tilly: customer needs short-term workaround — share code snippet for them to patch locally:

```
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)
scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 1024*64), 1024*1024*5) // 5MB max token
for scanner.Scan() {
  var evt Event
  if err := json.Unmarshal(scanner.Bytes(), &evt); err != nil { log.Printf("unmarshal: %v", err); continue }
  process(evt)
}
if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil { log.Printf("scanner err: %v", err) }
```

Or switch to json.Decoder as above.
mike: small note: if your objects can legitimately be >5MB consider a streaming JSON decoder approach that processes fields incrementally or change server to split large fields across events.
kevin: we've also seen cases where library versions mismatched — ACME is on `v0.2.0`. There's a newer patch `v0.3.1` that includes more robust stream reads + retry-on-early-eof for idempotent streams. Recommend upgrade.
acme-app: ok we'll try decoder and bump to v0.3.1. Any auth/billing implications? This is purely stream parsing, shouldn't affect billing.
mike: no billing change. If you see duplicate events after retries we'll look into idempotency keys.
tilly: I'll mark this as escalated to eng-go and eng-runtime. @mike can you follow up with a small SDK patch and a public support note?
mike: will open PR to add decoder fallback and expose `StreamOptions{MaxTokenSize:int}`. Target release: v0.3.1-rc1 today. Will also add tests that simulate chunked responses and proxy chunk boundaries.
deploy-bot: deploy started for staging (rollout/stream-parse-fallback) :rocket:
acme-app: thanks — trying the decoder now, will report back within the hour :crossed_fingers:
